result.summary:
LESSONS lane: why earlier fine-tuning lost, and guardrails for the AntiDeepfake (AD) partial fine-tune in work3/DESIGN.md. Numbers come from the repo's result files. Figures marked [measured] come from CPU checks I ran today.

## A. Per-attempt findings

**1. AST V2 / ep17 / full1029 (09-12..13). LB 0.6453 (ADS .6213, CPS .862) and 0.6175 (ADS .5881, CPS .8818), against G0 0.6909 (ADS .6578, CPS .9893).**
- Data: 1,029 files, split train 633 / dev 122 / gen-test 176 / src-test 98, with about 197 train groups. Voice was MLAAD-tiny and M-AILABS pairs; music was Echoes TTA against FMA; NSynth was the no-voice control.
- What was trained: AudioSet AST, last encoder block + LayerNorm + 5 heads (7.09M params). Head lr 1e-4, backbone lr 1e-5, batch 8x2, wd .01, clip 1. Ran 6 epochs, extended to 17 (stopped at 22). Augmentation was only crop and gain.
- Selection: partial-label proxy on the 122-file dev set. The dev proxy rose .866 -> .904 while the historical 274-file proxy went .7744 -> .7758 (flat). Both AST arms failed their own Voice gate and were submitted anyway.
- Why it lost:
  - Architecture swap: the AST-only package replaced the DF-Arena voice detector and PANNs presence. Presence collapse alone cost 0.1 x (.989 - .862) = -.0127 total.
  - Voice got worse.
  - Dev-proxy overfit.
  - Protocol breach (submitted after failing its own gate).
  - The full-data refit (no holdout) lost another -.028.
- Not the cause: the "only the first 10 s is scored" worry. `ast_multitask.py` covers the whole file with non-overlapping windows and averages them.

**2. V4 P1-P4 (09-13..14). Not submitted; the gate worked.**
- Full FT of SONICS and AST on 1,116 music rows. Encoder lr 1e-5..1e-4 (SONICS) and 1e-6..1e-5 (AST).
- Every arm had negative OOD gain (-.045 to -.117), including P3 with codec/noise augmentation.
- Duration alone was a shortcut: duration-only OOF AUC .894.

**3. V5 B1 (09-14). LB 0.6776, -0.013 vs G0, with several changes at once.**
- DF-Arena (an XLS-R-family model) fully fine-tuned on raw audio at lr 1e-6, 400 voice files per epoch, 5 of 60 epochs (time-cut). Dev Voice EER got worse, .150 -> .171.

**4. FullFT8 / S2_EAT (09-16). LB 0.6379 (ADS .5988), against M330 0.7396 (ADS .7119).**
- Data:
  - S1/S2 train had 474 files. Only 37 were real music, from one source (FMA), in 37 FMA-artist groups. The other 437 were Echoes renditions of those same songs, from about 9 generators.
  - Tune had 156 files (12 real); test had 190 files (12 real), all from the same sources.
  - S0 train had 918 files (61 real).
- What was trained: all MERT-330M or EAT layers including the conv stem. Encoder lr 1e-5, head lr 1e-4, wd .01, 5% warmup, at most 20 epochs with patience 3. 5-s clips, 4 random train windows per file, weighted sampler + CE, no augmentation, 1 seed.
- Selection: tune Music EER, then BCE.
- Evidence of overfit:
  - Train loss went .065 at epoch 4 -> .0006 at epoch 6.
  - Tune EER .014 vs test .168.
  - In the only controlled comparison (S0), full FT beat frozen MERT on tune (.230/.218 vs .246) but lost on test (.319/.300 vs .267).
- Calibration collapse [measured on its test_predictions.json]:
  - 90% of S2 EAT test predictions are above 0.99.
  - The 90th percentile of real-music scores is .998.
  - Both offline package probes scored .995 and .996.
- The packaged checkpoint was the S2 one, not refit. It differed from M330 only in the music branch: same DF-Arena voice, PANNs presence and max FILE rule. That music-only swap cost -0.113 ADS.
  - With voice unchanged, 0.3·ΔMusicEER + 0.5·ΔFileEER = 0.113. FILE EER must therefore have risen by at least about 0.05, unless M330's LB Music EER was below about 0.12.
- Most likely mechanism: the model learned source identity (FMA original vs Echoes rendition, 37 real songs). Selection was on data from the same sources. Its saturated fake scores then fed max(Pm·Fm, …), pushing FILE up for real music from unseen sources. A broken pipeline is unlikely: crop parity and exact tensor export were both verified.

**5. eight E7 LoRA (09-17). Never packaged, no LB score.**
- AD-1B with q/v LoRA r8/α16 on all 48 layers (1.97M params) + classifier. 200 updates, batch 2, lr 1e-4.
- Data: train 318/318 files from 3 speakers; dev 48/48 and test 48/48, 2 speakers each. Windows were zero-padded.
- Every arm had dev and test EER 0, so the comparison hit the ceiling and says nothing.
- Side signals:
  - LoRA-CE calibration thresholds were .998-.9998 (saturated); adding KL 0.1 to the frozen model kept them at .44-.79.
  - Frozen AD disagreed with 20% of the train labels.

**Common cause.** Prior full or near-full fine-tuning ran on hundreds of files with 1-37 real sources and was selected on data from the same sources. It memorized sources and produced saturated scores. Shipping decisions were not made against frozen models on held-out sources.

**What is different now.** Data v4 has 24,623 voice-labelled train rows, 10,583 components, 22 sources, 17 real sources and 358 fake (source, generator) cells: about 50x more rows than FullFT8.

## B. Guardrails for the AD partial FT
- **G1 Step-0 anchor (addition).** Before any update, run the eval code with the unmodified weights.
  - It must reproduce the zero-shot member on val: voice-route EER of window max = .1181 on 3,785 val rows.
  - The polarity check must hold: fake is index 0, AUC > 0.5.
  - An export -> `antideepfake_runtime.AntiDeepfake` reload of the unmodified model must pass `verify_native`. That proves the inverse key mapping, including pos_conv weight_g/weight_v.
- **G2 Right baseline, early kill (addition).** The model to beat is frozen AD + trained head, not the zero-shot classifier (.118).
  - Frozen-feature heads reach val .0485 (S3 Linear) and .039-.044 (MLP) [measured].
  - If ft val voice EER is not below about .045 by the end of epoch 1, stop and don't package.
  - For head training on AD features, about 0.8 of the val gain carried over to held-out, and held-out EER sits well above val (linear head .056 val vs .136 held-out).
- **G3 Selection (consistent; carving rejected).** Keep DESIGN's selection on val.
  - [measured] Picking the epoch on val landed within .001 (Linear) and .010 (MLP) of the best held-out epoch.
  - A set carved from train with held-out generator families (val_ood) tracked held-out no better (Spearman −0.24 for MLP), so don't carve one.
  - Also report val EER on rows with at least 64,600 samples: 26% of val rows are shorter than one window, but competition test files are all 4 s or longer.
  - Caveat: these heads cannot memorize sources the way roughly 315M trainable parameters can, which is why G4-G8 still matter.
- **G4 Sampler cap (DEVIATION).** DESIGN's WeightedRandomSampler (with replacement, loss_weights × duration_balance) over-draws a few rows badly [measured over 24,623 train rows]:
  - Median row: 0.36 draws per epoch; 99th percentile 5.5; maximum 74.
  - 39 real rows, the ones FullFT8-style memorization would target: existing:FMA/FMA 9 rows at 59x per epoch, existing:constructed_music 13 rows at 43x, constructed_enhanced 17 rows at 43x. Over 4 epochs that is about 170-240 exposures each. constructed_enhanced is the worst held-out cell (25% FPR).
  - 7.4% of all draws go to rows drawn 20 or more times per epoch; 9.8% of rows are expected fewer than 0.1 times per epoch.
  - Fix: clip per-row expected draws at 4 per epoch and renormalize. This leaves real-class mass at .446 instead of .50. The alternative is no-replacement sampling with loss weights, the repo's head-training convention.
- **G5 Train/runtime parity (trainer lane).**
  - Set `layerdrop=0`. The config has 0.1; HF skips whole layers in train mode, including frozen ones, and randomly skipped trainable layers break DDP.
  - Keep `apply_spec_augment=False`, as the runtime does (the config has mask_time_prob .075).
  - Put the feature extractor, projection and layers 0-31 in `eval()` so their 0.1 dropout is off.
  - Compute every member CSV with `AntiDeepfake(export_dir).windows(voice)` in fp32 from the exported fp16 file, not from the in-memory model.
  - Treat voice_silent as runtime does (score 0).
  - Measure the effect of fp16 stems against runtime fp32 stems on the 10 parity files; tolerance 1e-3 in prob.
- **G6 Saturation (addition).**
  - Evidence: S2 EAT had 90% of scores above .99. Zero-shot AD max already has 35% of val rows above .9999, and only 76% of the values are unique. The MLP head's saturated share grew from 0 to 18% by epoch 30 [measured].
  - The voice fusion maps each score through a val CDF (`np.interp` on a 1001-point quantile table), so tied scores collapse to one value and lose their ranking.
  - Write fp32 fake log-odds (logit0 − logit1) alongside the probabilities, and build the CDF tables on log-odds. For max this is the same ordering apart from ties.
  - Report the share of unique ft_max values on val and held-out; flag it below 0.95.
  - The runtime would need `windows()` to return logits (integration lane).
- **G7 Epochs (consistent).**
  - Keep: at most 4 epochs, evaluation every 1/4 epoch, patience 3.
  - Add: log train CE, val CE and saturated share at each eval. Choose checkpoints by (val EER, val CE), the repo convention.
  - Add: stop if val CE rises for 3 evals in a row. Val EER on in-source data plateaus while CE detects the overconfidence seen in AST and FullFT8.
- **G8 Held-out vs frozen (addition, stricter than DESIGN).**
  - Report held-out once, for three models: the zero-shot AD member, the S4-equivalent with the frozen-AD head, and the ft member.
  - Break it down per held-out cell, each at its own val-EER threshold: FLEURS-ko, constructed_enhanced, constructed_mix and MUSAN reals (FPR); HAIM, VoxCPM, OpenVoice and MLAAD fakes (miss rate).
  - Veto shipping if any real-cell FPR worsens by 0.05 or more absolute, even if the +0.01 ADS gate passes. Real content from an unseen source scored as fake is exactly how FullFT8 lost.
- **G9 Protocol (consistent).** Write the selection rule and gate thresholds to a lock file before scoring held-out, as R2 did with choice_lock.json. No variants added after held-out is opened (the AST hybrid and E08 did this). Single-seed held-out noise is about ±.01 EER [measured on the MLP curve].
- **G10 Depth and lr (consistent).** There is no in-repo evidence against freezing layers 0-31 or against backbone lr 1e-5. The update budget is about 4 x 24,623/128 ≈ 770 updates, about 4 window exposures per row. Label smoothing or KL to the frozen model is optional; adopting either would deviate from DESIGN's "plain CE".

## C. Where this contradicts DESIGN.md
- **G4 (sampler)** is the one real deviation.
- **Padding rationale is inaccurate.** DESIGN says to repeat-pad short clips "like baseline extract_segment". The AD runtime (`windows`/`predict`) instead feeds sub-window files at native length, with no padding. That matters for 33% of train rows (38% of fakes vs 22% of reals), 26% of val and 5% of held-out. Repeat padding is fine for training only; evaluation must use the runtime path.
- **G8 veto** is stricter than DESIGN's gate but does not conflict with it.
- **Not a deviation:** carving a separate selection set from train was tested and rejected, so DESIGN's selection on val stands.
result.how_to_run:
Nothing from this lane needs to run on VESSL. The diagnostic is CPU-only and needs the project tree plus the local _workspace/backbone_cache. Paths resolve relative to the project root through data_v4/train_backbone_heads.py (BANK, AD); nothing is a hard-coded Mac path.

Local run (from the project root):
  .venv/bin/python research/top15/work3/lessons/val_proxy_check.py --cache _workspace/backbone_cache --out research/top15/work3/lessons/val_proxy_check.json --epochs 30

On a Linux box with the same tree:
  /root/envs/data/bin/python research/top15/work3/lessons/val_proxy_check.py --cache <backbone_cache> --out <out.json>

Optional flag: --arch linear mlp. Runtime is about 1 min on 4 threads, peak RSS 1.8 GB.

Hooks for the trainer and integration lanes:
- G1 anchor: target val voice-route EER of window max = 0.1181 over the 3,785 voice-labelled val rows, per _workspace/members_20260927/members_all.csv.
- G4 cap: clip per-row expected draws at 4 per epoch and renormalize: w = min(w, 4·mean(w)), repeat until stable.
result.risks:
- **G3 is indirect evidence.** It rests on heads over frozen AD features (at most about 0.3M parameters), not on the fine-tune itself. The roughly 315M trainable parameters in layers 32-47 can memorize sources the way FullFT8 did; the diagnostic cannot show that. Its val_ood set was also small: 2,337 rows from 4 fake generators and 2 real sources. So "carving doesn't help" is only weakly supported.
- **Held-out was used in the diagnostic.** It served only to judge whether val is a sound selection signal, never to choose a model or checkpoint. That is a mild protocol exposure, to be noted in the DB-protocol record.
- **FullFT8's File-EER damage is inferred, not observed.** The official breakdown by component isn't available. The "FILE got worse by at least about 0.05" conclusion is arithmetic that assumes M330's LB Music EER was at least about 0.12.
- **eight_lora never reached the LB,** so its only lessons are the saturation and teacher-disagreement signals.
- **G4 sampler numbers use backbone_cache sample counts** for duration_balance, which may differ slightly from the counts in /root/stems.
- **Not measured:** the effect of fp16 stems, and whether repeat padding vs native length changes the score for short clips.
- **Thresholds are judgement calls:** the .045 kill value, the ±0.05 per-cell FPR veto and the 0.95 unique-value flag are heuristics taken from the repo's noise levels (single-seed held-out noise about ±.01 EER), not tuned values.
result.smoke_evidence:
- **Environment:** val_proxy_check.py ran on CPU (Apple, torch 4 threads) in 58.7 s wall, peak RSS 1.78 GB, exit 0.
- **Rows used:** train 22,286 (after carving) / val_ood 2,337 / val 3,785 / test 5,139 voice rows.
- **Parity sanity check:** at epoch 0, the linear head (the unmodified AD classifier on cached embeddings) scored val .11806 and test .18779. The zero-shot members_all.csv xlsr1b_max gives .1181 and .1878, so the cached path matches the member scores.
- **Linear head:** val .118 -> .055. Test was best at .1356 (epoch 5 and epoch 30); the val-picked epoch 28 gave .1366. Spearman over epochs: val vs test 0.29; val_ood vs test 0.38.
- **MLP head:**
  - Val and val_ood both picked epoch 8, which gave test .1243; the best test value was .1144 at epoch 30.
  - Spearman: val vs test 0.43; val_ood vs test −0.24.
  - Share of saturated probabilities (p > 1−1e-6) grew from 0 to 18% on val and 10% on test by epochs 28-30.
- **Other checks:** FullFT8 prediction saturation, zero-shot AD saturation and tie rates, sampler repeat statistics and short-clip shares were computed with inline .venv scripts. The results are quoted in the summary; no files were modified.

review.issues:
Full critique: /Users/choiwuseck/Documents/ChatGPT/데이콘/research/top15/work3/lessons/critique.md. I ran two CPU checks; the scripts are in scratchpad lessons_skeptic/check1_stats.py and check2_precision.py.

The summary I was given stops mid-G8, so nothing after that point was reviewed. The lessons folder also has no written guardrail file, only the val_proxy_check diagnostic.

**F1 (high): G1's "export -> reload must pass verify_native" cannot pass.**
- (a) verify_native needs native_reference.json and parity_audio.npz. Neither exists anywhere in the project, and the listed VESSL folder /root/models/xlsr1b does not have them either, so the call raises FileNotFoundError.
- (b) Even with those files, fp16 export of the UNMODIFIED weights moves logits by up to 6.9e-3 [measured on the 10 parity files]. That is well above verify_native's atol 3e-4.

**F2 (medium): the step-0 anchor ".1181 must reproduce" conflicts with the trainer's default eval precision.**
- The trainer evaluates with `--eval-precision bf16` by default, and evaluate(0) runs under bf16.
- CPU bf16 autocast moved window log-odds by up to 0.46 and fake prob by up to 0.006 [measured]. So step 0 will not equal .11806 exactly.
- The trainer's val set also depends on which stems exist, so a fixed number is the wrong target.
- The G2 kill and G7 selection carry the same bf16 noise.

**F3 (medium): tolerances in probability space are ill-posed.**
- This covers G5's 1e-3 prob tolerance and the trainer's round-trip check (`ok: diff <= 1e-3`).
- fp16 rounding shifts log-odds by 0.013, which is about 3e-3 in probability near p = 0.5. A correct checkpoint could fail the round trip.

**F4 (medium): G6's "windows() must return logits" is unnecessary.**
- `windows()` already returns the pooled fp32 embedding, so the caller can compute `classifier(emb)`.
- Only integration code changes; antideepfake_runtime.py stays as it is.

**F5 (medium): G3 is overstated.**
- Spearman correlation with held-out across epochs: val .285 (Linear) / .429 (MLP); val_ood .384 (Linear) / −.244 (MLP).
- For the Linear head, val_ood tracked held-out better and picked the best held-out epoch.
- "Val pick within .001/.010 of the best held-out epoch" reflects flat held-out curves, not val tracking held-out.

**F6 (low-medium, missed by the lane): short clips are handled differently in training and eval.**
- Training tiles clips shorter than 64,600 samples (`np.tile`), while `windows()`, and so val and the runtime, scores the unpadded short clip.
- 26.2% of val voice rows are shorter than one window (72% of them fake); on held-out it is 5.0%. So about a quarter of val EER comes from an input shape the model never trained on and the competition test does not contain.
- The test minimum is 64,000 samples, not 64,600. Only 20 val rows fall between the two, so that part is negligible.

**F7 (low): the A.4 arithmetic is wrong.**
- For FILE EER to have risen by at least 0.05, M330's Music EER must be at least about 0.21, not 0.12.
- If it was 0.12, the bound on the FILE EER rise is about 0.

**F8 (low): G4 per-cell figures are rounded; the headline stats reproduce exactly.**
- Draws per epoch: constructed_music 41-74 and constructed_enhanced 25-60 (the summary says 43 for both).
- Clipping at 4 and renormalizing gives a max of 4.51, with 618 rows above 4. Real-class mass is .449, not .446.

**F9 (low): G8's per-cell veto has no cell sizes and no paired test.**

**F10 (low): diagnostic hygiene.**
- `mlp.test_frozen` in the JSON is a random-init MLP, not a frozen reference.
- Held-out was scored 62 times and informed the G2/G3 thresholds. Disclose this.

**F11 (low): DESIGN's ±6 dB gain augmentation is a no-op.** AntiDeepfake.forward layer-normalizes each window, which removes any gain change.

**F12 (info, cross-lane): size and runtime.**
- Integration loads a separate AntiDeepfake for each nonzero member.
- If the fusion keeps both 'ad' and 'ft', the package holds two ~1.93 GB models and runs AD twice per file on L4.

**Verified OK:**
- Splits: 0 components and 0 groups shared across train, val and test.
- Counts: 24,623 / 3,785 / 5,139 voice rows, all in backbone_cache; 10,583 components, 22 sources, 17 real sources, 358 fake cells.
- Anchor: val EER .11806 (AUC .944 with index 0 = fake) and held-out .18779 reproduce from members_all.csv. They equal linear-head epoch 0, so cache embeddings match the runtime member.
- Saturation: 34.9% of val rows above .9999, 76.1% unique values.
- G5 config facts: layerdrop .1, mask_time_prob .075, dropout .1.
- Trainer: keeps the encoder module in eval and excludes pos_conv_embed and masked_spec_embed from the trainable set, so there is no DDP unused-parameter crash. Per-rank sampler seeds mean no cross-rank duplication. Targets use class 0 = fake. Max |w| 5.64, so no fp16 overflow.
review.fixes:
**G1** Replace the verify_native gate with three checks:
1. The key-set check that save_native already does (no missing or extra keys).
2. Reload the export and compare it to the in-memory model with weights rounded to fp16. This should agree to float noise and proves the key mapping.
3. Compare to fp32 with a log-odds tolerance of at most 0.05.

Define the step-0 anchor against members_all.csv xlsr1b_max on the trainer's actual val IDs. Run it with --eval-precision fp32, or allow |ΔEER| ≤ 0.003 under bf16. Confirm the final chosen checkpoint in fp32.

**G5 and the trainer round-trip check:** state tolerances in log-odds (≤ 0.05) rather than probability.

**G6:** compute log-odds from the embedding windows() already returns (classifier(emb)); leave antideepfake_runtime.py unchanged.

**G3:** rephrase as "no evidence that carving helps; val tracking is weak (Spearman ≤ .43)". Make val EER on rows of at least 64,000 samples the G2 kill metric and a co-metric for selection (a deviation from DESIGN; flag it).

**G4:** use the exact per-cell ranges, iterate the clip or state the cap as about 4.5, and put real-class mass at .449.

**G8:** report n per cell and veto only when a paired, group-level bootstrap shows the worsening beyond its 90% CI.

**A.4:** correct the threshold to about 0.21.

**Diagnostic JSON:** drop `mlp.test_frozen` and disclose the held-out use.

**Integration:** enforce weight['ad'] = 0 when 'ft' ships, or re-time and re-size the package.

result.summary:
I built the Track C trainer in research/top15/work3/trainer/ and did not change DESIGN.md. The CPU smoke run on real HTDemucs stems passes every check the task asked for. Nothing has run on a GPU yet.

**What each file does**
- **finetune_ad.py**
  - Runs under torchrun/DDP on NCCL. Without torchrun it runs as a single process, and the CPU smoke uses gloo.
  - Builds the model with the project's own antideepfake_runtime.AntiDeepfake, so the architecture and key mapping match the runtime exactly. It then freezes everything except encoder layers 32..47, encoder.encoder.layer_norm and the classifier. That is 314.8M trainable params out of 962.5M, which the smoke confirms.
  - Frozen modules stay in eval mode, so there is no layerdrop and no dropout below layer 32. Trainable layers use the config's dropout of 0.1.
  - Dataset: voice rows chosen with head_labels semantics, re-implemented and matching full_bank_train.read_items (a music-route row whose voice stem is silent is dropped; a voice-route row is kept). Each item is one random 64600-sample crop of the voice stem; shorter clips are repeat-padded like baseline extract_segment. Class 0 is fake.
  - Sampling uses WeightedRandomSampler with loss_weights x duration_balance, from a byte-identical copy of full_bank_batches.py. Loss is plain cross-entropy.
  - Augmentation runs on the GPU as DESIGN.md specifies (telephone 300-3400 Hz via 8 kHz p .15, FIR low-pass 3.4-8 kHz p .3, white/pink noise SNR 10-40 dB p .5, gain +-6 dB, random polarity).
  - Training uses bf16 autocast, AdamW param groups (1e-5 backbone / 1e-4 head, wd .01), cosine schedule with 5% warmup, and grad clip 1.0 that raises on a non-finite value.
  - Eval runs at step 0 (the zero-shot baseline) and then every quarter epoch on val voice rows. It uses AntiDeepfake.predict's window layout (hop 32300 plus a tail window; a file shorter than one window is a single clip with no padding), fake prob at softmax index 0, file max, and silent stems scored 0. EER comes from graph_scoring._roc_metrics; the best eval is picked by (EER, BCE); training stops after 3 evals with no improvement or at 4 epochs.
  - The best checkpoint goes to RUN/best: fp16 safetensors with every native key (proj_fc.*, m_ssl.model.*, and the 7 training-only tensors copied from the base file). It is written one tensor at a time and swapped into place atomically.
  - At the end, rank 0 runs two checks and writes them to result.json:
    - Parameter check: fp64 fingerprints before and after training show every changed tensor is in the trainable set.
    - Round trip: rank 0 reloads RUN/best with the unmodified AntiDeepfake class, checks the weights equal fp16(trained weights) exactly, and compares window probabilities with fp32 reference probabilities saved at checkpoint time.
- **score_ft.py**: shards rows across GPUs under torchrun (gloo is used only for the barrier) and loads the checkpoint with AntiDeepfake itself. It runs in fp32 by default to match the L4 runtime (--bf16 for speed) and writes ID,ft_max,ft_top30,ft_mean,voice_silent for every row in manifest order. Values are raw for all rows, silent ones included, like members_all.csv.
- **run_ft.sh**: runs the 4-GPU training, then asserts the hard invariants (exact weights on reload, no frozen tensor changed), then scores val and test into ft_members.csv.
- **smoke_test.py**: the one runnable check that reproduces the smoke evidence below.

**Choices not spelled out in DESIGN.md**
- Selection eval runs in bf16 (--eval-precision fp32 is available); the member CSV is fp32.
- The zero-shot step-0 eval can be kept as "best" if fine-tuning never beats it, which is an honest negative result.
- One epoch = one crop per train voice item: 24,623 items give 193 steps at a global batch of 128.

**H100 throughput estimate from FLOPs**
- FLOPs were measured on meta-device replicas: 414.7 GFLOP per 4.04 s window forward and 674.2 GFLOP per training window. That is 21.6 TFLOP per 32-window GPU step.
- At 25-40% MFU (989 TFLOP/s bf16 peak) that is 11.5-18.3 steps/s per GPU, or about 1.5k-2.3k windows/s on 4 GPUs.
- The default 770 steps take about 42-67 s of compute.
- One val eval (bf16) is 12,883 windows, about 5.3 PFLOP, roughly 10 s including 984 single-clip forwards. The default run does up to 17 evals, about 3 min.
- Scoring val+test in fp32 is 57,441 windows, about 23.8 PFLOP, roughly 2-3 min (about 20 s with --bf16).
- Window counts come from the exact sample counts in _workspace/backbone_cache.
- Expected total wall time is about 8-12 min, including 4 x 3.86 GB model loads and checkpoint writes of 1.93 GB each.
- The data loader then has to supply about 1.2k-2.3k npz reads/s (roughly 0.3-0.55 GB/s).

**Flag for the orchestrator:** training compute is only about 1 minute. The 4-epoch cap (each epoch sees one 4 s crop per file, about 1.2 passes over the voice audio in total) will probably stop training before early stopping triggers. I left the design value as the default; --max-epochs changes it.
result.how_to_run:
VESSL (Linux, 4 x H100). Copy the trainer/ folder to e.g. /root/ft/trainer. Bank CSVs are expected at /root/ft/bank_trainval.csv and /root/ft/bank_test.csv (override with BANK_TV / BANK_TEST).

  bash /root/ft/trainer/run_ft.sh /root/ft/runs/ftC1
  # env overrides: PY=/root/envs/data/bin/python NPROC=4 STEMS=/root/stems MODEL=/root/models/xlsr1b CODE=/root/ft/code WORKERS=10
  # extra args go to finetune_ad.py, e.g.: bash run_ft.sh /root/ft/runs/ftC2 --max-epochs 12 --eval-every 96

Outputs in OUT:
- train.log, metrics.jsonl (setup/train/eval/result records), evals.json
- result.json (best, zero_shot, params audit, roundtrip)
- val_best.csv
- best/ (model.safetensors fp16 in native layout + antideepfake_config.json + meta.json)
- score.log, ft_members.csv (val+test: ID,ft_max,ft_top30,ft_mean,voice_silent)

Pieces run separately:

result.risks:
- **No GPU evidence yet.** Everything was verified on CPU with fp32 training, first trainable layer 46 (to fit the RAM cap), batch 4, no augmentation in the overfit, and a 1-process gloo DDP. Not yet exercised: bf16 autocast, NCCL with 4 ranks, the default layer-32 freeze in real training, GPU peak memory, loader throughput from /root/stems, and the actual val gain. result.json reports peak_gpu_gb and the train/eval seconds.
- **fp16 checkpoint drift.** Casting to fp16 is lossless in layout, and weights_exact is checked, but predictions still move slightly:
  - Real-audio members drifted at most 2.4e-4 in the smoke, which is within 1e-3.
  - A synthetic all-zero silent stem drifted 1.4e-3. The runtime scores silent stems 0, so this does not affect results.
  - run_ft.sh hard-fails only on weights_exact or a changed frozen tensor. Prob drift above 1e-3 on the 16 reference files sets roundtrip.ok=false without stopping the run.
  - ft_members.csv is computed from the fp16 checkpoint itself, so fusion tables fitted on it match what the L4 runtime computes.
- **Train/eval mismatch on short files.** In training, clips under 4.04 s are repeat-padded (per DESIGN), while eval and the runtime score them unpadded at native length. That is 33% of train voice items and 26% of val.
- **Stems are fp16.** Members are computed from fp16-rounded voice stems; the runtime uses fp32 stems. The difference should be negligible but has not been measured on the bank.
- **Gain is a no-op.** The +-6 dB gain augmentation has no effect because AntiDeepfake layer-normalises the waveform.
- **Likely under-training at the design cap.** 4 epochs is about 770 steps and 1.2 passes over the voice audio; see the flag above.
- **Selection vs final numerics.** Selection uses bf16 eval (switchable) while the member CSV is fp32, so val EER in evals.json can differ slightly from EER recomputed from ft_members.csv.
- **Missing stems are skipped silently.** Rows without a stem are dropped and counted (setup.missing_stems, and the score_ft summary line) rather than failing the run.
- **No resume support.** The whole run is estimated at about 10 minutes.
- **Eval cost.** Up to 17 checkpoint writes of 1.93 GB go to OUT. Rank 0 does the save while the other ranks wait at the next all-reduce, which is fine within the 10-minute NCCL timeout. The 984 short val files run as single-clip forwards; cudnn.benchmark stays off, as the runtime sets it, to avoid re-tuning for every new clip length.
- **CPU RAM cap.** The single-process trainer peaked at a 4.82 GB footprint and score_ft at 5.10 GB (/usr/bin/time -l), but only with 4-window eval batches.
  - The default 64-window batch on CPU reaches about 9.7 GB, from the fp16-to-fp32 load (about 4.2 GB) plus activations. That is irrelevant on H100 but matters for any local run.
  - The torchrun smoke itself was not memory-profiled: psutil cannot read child-process memory on macOS.
- **Rendezvous.** On macOS, `torchrun --standalone` hung resolving the host name, so both scripts use a static rendezvous on 127.0.0.1 (ports 29531/29532). If those ports are in use on VESSL, edit run_ft.sh.

review.issues:
The trainer is OK to run on GPU. I found no correctness bug in labels, splits, test leakage, fake-index polarity, key layout, freezing or DDP mechanics. Two design-level risks and two cheap missing gates remain. Full write-up: /Users/choiwuseck/Documents/ChatGPT/데이콘/research/top15/work3/trainer/critique.md

Checks run (scripts in scratchpad ft_skeptic/):
- **Check 1: bank CSVs, using the trainer's own functions.**
  - Split values: train 30,658 / val 4,931 / test 6,450, so `--splits val test` matches.
  - No ID, component or group overlap between train, val and test.
  - Voice items: 24,623 train (3,328 mixed rows, none dropped as silent, no silent voice-route stems) and 3,785 val.
  - The zero-shot anchor reproduces exactly: val EER 0.11806, test 0.18779.
- **Check 2: 2-rank gloo DDP run of the real finetune_ad.main**, on a tiny random model in the native fairseq key layout and the real smoke stems.
  - Ranks draw different items and crops.
  - The sharded eval collects all 29 windows, with none lost or duplicated.
  - Early stopping stops both ranks at the same step, and the final barrier exits cleanly.
  - No frozen tensor changed, and the checkpoint reloads with weights_exact=true.

Findings:
1. **Design risk, as DESIGN specifies:** WeightedRandomSampler turns loss_weights × duration_balance into heavy repetition.
   - Over 4 epochs (98,816 draws), the effective sample size is only 4,211 of 24,623 items.
   - The top item is expected about 297 times; 524 items appear 20 or more times.
   - 4,165 items (17%) are expected fewer than 0.5 times.
   - MLAAD fakes take 32.5% of all draws.
   - With a 315M-parameter backbone, this risks memorisation in a way the frozen-head trainer never had.
2. **Design risk:** random 4.04 s crops of song voice stems (3,328 mixed rows, 17.5% of sampling mass) can land in instrumental passages yet still carry the file's voice label. Because the member is the file max, this can cause false positives on real songs. It could not be quantified locally (event_intervals is empty for these rows).
3. **Gate gap:** missing stems are silently tolerated.
   - The trainer records the count but keeps training.
   - score_ft skips rows without stems.
   - run_ft.sh asserts neither.
   - An incomplete /root/stems would bias the held-out gate onto a subset.
4. **Packaging:** the S4 zip is 8.296 GB and already holds the frozen AD in fp16 (1.931 GB).
   - Replacing it with the ft checkpoint keeps the package at about 8.3 GB.
   - Keeping both gives about 10.23 GB, which is over the 10 GB limit.
   - The runtime should use `AntiDeepfake.windows()[1]`, not `predict()`, which raises on clips under 400 samples.
5. **bf16 selection vs fp32 members:** selection evals run in bf16, members in fp32. Compare the step-0 val EER with 0.11806; if they differ by more than about 0.003, use --eval-precision fp32. val_best.csv holds bf16 values, so downstream code must use ft_members.csv.
6. **Minor:**
   - The default run is 772 steps and 18 evals, not 770 and 17.
   - Each improving eval makes rank 0 write a 1.93 GB checkpoint while the other ranks wait, so the output folder should be on local disk.
   - The checkpoint directory swap is not atomic.
   - Nothing checks for inf/NaN when saving, so an fp16 overflow would still pass the weights check.
   - Short-clip repeat-padding in training differs from eval, as already flagged.
   - Val is used both for checkpoint selection and for fusion fitting.
   - The held-out gain should be reported separately for sources AntiDeepfake saw in pretraining and those it did not.

Not verified: NCCL with 4 ranks, CUDA bf16 numerics, peak GPU memory, loader throughput, save/reload time on VESSL storage, and any real accuracy gain.

result.summary:
The integration for adding the fine-tuned AntiDeepfake member "ft" to S4 is staged in research/top15/work3/integration/. No project files were edited. Every piece reproduces S4 exactly where it should, and the plumbing was proven on CPU with a stand-in ft (the frozen zero-shot AntiDeepfake scores from members_1b.csv). The one thing not run is the full package at runtime (verify_datav4_submission.py): it needs more than 10 GB of RAM, over my 6 GB limit. The exact steps are in how_to_run.

What was built:
1. fit_ft_fusion.py has two modes.
   - `db` is the DB-protocol gate. It reads the S4-equivalent member scores in work2/stacking (runs/*.json, presence_*.json, frozen_rows.json) plus the ft CSVs. For option R (VOICE = fuse(ours 1, ft w)) and option A (fuse(ours 1, ad 0.5, ft w)) it picks w from {0.5, 1, 2} on val official ADS under runtime semantics (RT), refitting the FILE ensemble for every configuration. It then picks the option with the higher val RT ADS (tie goes to R).
   - Only after that choice does `db` compute held-out official ADS in both RT and AC (R2-pipeline) semantics, plus a group bootstrap vs S4 (1000 reps, test group_id, rng 0). It applies the DESIGN gate (RT dADS >= +0.01 and P(>0) >= 0.95).
   - `db` aborts unless the S4 baseline reproduces RT 0.93773/0.88457 and AC 0.93845/0.88643, and unless the bootstrap ADS equals the official ADS.
   - `p1` is the package fit. It takes the S4 P1 heads, the local caches for all 4,931 val rows and the ft val CSV. It writes a heads dir with component_fusion.json, the refitted file_ensemble.json, the lock, identity and metrics, usable as both --heads and --fusion for the packager. In R it drops voice_ad_*.pt. `p1 --option S4` must reproduce S4 and aborts otherwise. It refuses any ft column other than ft_max, because the runtime only computes the window max.
2. Staged full_bank_submission.py: the fusion setup moves into `Engine.load_fusion` and the per-file fusion into `Engine.fused_voice`. Members are 'ad' (frozen detector plus ResMLP heads, unchanged) and 'ft' (the fine-tuned detector's window-max fake probability). Each detector loads from assets/antideepfake/<member>. An unknown fusion member raises SubmissionError instead of being silently skipped by fuse(). For an S4 fusion the operations are identical to the current runtime.
3. Staged package_datav4_submission.py adds --mert-fp16: the base MERT bin is re-stored as fp16, and packaging is refused unless every fp32 tensor round-trips exactly. Detector weights are now streamed rather than held in memory, and members are re-hashed from the zip in chunks. The existing member-name-to-directory logic already covers R ({ft}) and A ({ad, ft}).
4. component_fusion.py needs no change: fuse() works with any member names, and 'ft' ran through it in every test. No staged copy.
5. Three helper scripts:
   - check_mert_fp16.py checks that an fp16 MERT bin loads into the same fp32 model and outputs.
   - ft_runtime_parity.py compares packaged-runtime predictions with the offline path on the 10 parity files.
   - smoke_runtime.py is the CPU plumbing test of the runtime methods.

Results with the stand-in:
- The gate correctly fails for both options, which matches the earlier rejection of zero-shot AntiDeepfake fusion. R at w=0.5 gives held-out RT 0.86968 (dADS -0.01489); A at w=0.5 gives 0.87616 (dADS -0.00841). The val rule chose A at w=0.5 (val RT 0.92991 vs R 0.92298); P(>0) is 0.0 for both.
- Package sizes: option A (frozen ad + ft fp16 + fp16 MERT) is 9,595,957,456 B, 0.404 GB under 10 GB. Option R is 8,288,341,878 B, 7.3 MB smaller than S4.
- The fp16 MERT bin loads under transformers 4.57.6 (the DACON version) into fp32 weights bitwise identical to the fp32 bin.

Two deviations to flag:
- **Option R directory name:** the fine-tuned weights live under model/assets/antideepfake/ft, not .../ad as the task text says. Same size; the frozen 'ad' directory is simply absent.
- **Option choice:** DESIGN.md defines only R. I added A and the val rule that picks between them. For an R-only reading, use boot_vs_S4['R<w>|RT'] in the report.
